summary: Tsering Shakya is a scholar in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He earned his BA, MPhil, and PhD from SOAS University of London, where he was a research fellow (1999–2002), taught at Oxford, and held a research chair at the University of British Columbia.

Tsewang Gyurme works in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He has served as president of the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences and as president of the Tibetan Association for Sacred Studies (attested 2006).

Tsikey Chokling Rinpoche was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology educated at Young Lamas Home School. He served as master of Vajrayana ceremonies at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling (~1976–2020) and was a board member of Rangjung Yeshe Shenpen (~2003–2020).

Tso Sze-bong is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed his PhD at the Australian National University (1977–1982) under doctoral supervisors Jan Willem de Jong and Tissa Rajapatirana.

Tsoknyi Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied at Khampagar Monastery and under teachers including Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje, Dilgo Khyentse, and Adeu Rinpoche. He founded the Pundarika Foundation and held a post at Tergar Osel Ling Monastery.

Tsuguhito Takeuchi was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at Kyoto University and Indiana University (PhD 1980–1994), where his doctoral supervisor was Christopher I. Beckwith, and served as Professor of Linguistics at Kobe City University of Foreign Studies (~1999–2017).

Tsugunari Kubo was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Tokyo and earned a doctorate from Rissho University. He served as president of Reiyukai and of the International Institute for Buddhist Studies, which he founded.
Tsui Lan Liza Cheung is a Buddhist studies scholar. She earned her PhD from The University of Hong Kong (attested 2013) under doctoral supervisor K. L. Dhammajoti and studied under Toshiichi Endo.

Tsukasa Mizushima is an Indology and history scholar who earned his degrees, including a doctorate, from the University of Tokyo. He held faculty posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies and was a professor at the University of Tokyo (1997–2018).

Tsultrim Gyatso was active in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He served as a senior instructor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and as abbot of Drepung Gomang Dratsang (attested 1987).

Tsultrim Kelsang is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts as lecturer (attested 1984) and professor (attested 1999–2002) at Otani University, and served as a visiting researcher at Ryukoku University in 2015.

Tsuneki Nishiwaki is a scholar of Sinology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who studied at Tokyo University of Education (~1962–1971). He held positions at Doshisha University (~1973–1993) and served as professor at Kyoto University (~1993–2007).
Tsutomu Hatai was an Indology figure who served as president of the Ayurveda Research Society, where he was attested in 1987 having succeeded Hiroshi Maruyama.

Tsutomu Kubo was a philosophy scholar who studied under Raphael von Koeber at the University of Tokyo and earned a doctorate from Tohoku University. He served on the faculties of the University of Tokyo, Tohoku University (professor 1940–1946), and Toyo University (~1949–1954).
Tsutomu Yamaguchi is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied at Hokkaido University. He held an affiliated researcher post at the Eastern Institute (attested 2015).

Tsuyoshi Yokoyama is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Kyoto University (attested 2015–2017) and served as a specially appointed researcher at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2017).

Tu Weiming is a scholar of philosophy, Sinology, and religious studies who earned his MA and PhD from Harvard University. He held faculty posts at Berkeley and Harvard (1981–2010), directed the Harvard-Yenching Institute (1996–2008), and became chair professor at Peking University (~2010).

Tubten Chokyi Dorje was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo. He taught prominent students, including Dilgo Khyentse, Chatral Sangye Dorje, and Khenpo Shenga.
Tubten Gyeltsen Ozer studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Tubten Nyendrak was a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Khenpo Shenga, and he taught Botrul Dongak Tenpai Nyima and Dodrupchen Rinpoche.
